description: Synthetic world for the fictional company Globex. Exists to prove per-tenant isolation (demo moment 6). Deliberately shares PROJECT NAMES with Acme but nothing else, so the same question reaches a genuinely different answer rather than an empty graph.

agents.name: Planner
agents.role: Turns user intent into decisions and tasks

agents.name: Reviewer
agents.role: Checks requests against remembered decisions and acts

sessions.note: Bootstrap container, same role as Acme's.

events.summary: Company structure imported from onboarding records: people, projects, systems and their relationships.
Billing v2 cleared for independent release; it was deliberately decoupled from Spring Launch.

decisions.title: Release Billing v2 independently of Spring Launch
decisions.reason: Globex decoupled billing from the launch train so finance work could ship on its own cadence.
decisions.note: PLANTED. This is the isolation contrast. Asked 'can we ship the billing feature?', Acme blocks (Billing v2 depends on a delayed Spring Launch) and Globex clears it (explicitly decoupled). Same question, opposite answer, and the reason is readable in each graph.

facts.note: Globex has a dependency too, just not on Billing v2. Keeps the contrast honest: the different answer comes from a different graph shape, not from Globex being empty.
